Veeam.title: On-premises AI vs. cloud AI: The data protection trade-offs nobody budgets in
Veeam.summary: Every comparison of on-premises AI and cloud AI evaluates the same four things: Cost, latency, scalability, and control. Almost no one evaluates who restores the data when something breaks. That gap matters more than the comparison does, because on-premises AI (e.g., the full model lifecycle on infrastructure you own) and cloud AI (e.g., that same capability consumed as a service) both change where your data sits without changing who carries the recovery obligation. Cisco.title: Vulnerabilities in nginx Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
Cisco.summary: On November 18, 2026, nginx announced the availability of a fix for multiple critical vulnerabilities in nginx that could lead to remote code execution. These vulnerabilities affect nginx releases 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 and is fixed in releases 1.31.9 (mainline) and 1.30.7 (stable). These vulnerabilities were identified by the following CVEs: CVE-2026-113425: NGINX ngx_mail_proxy_module vulnerability CVE-2026-121810: NGINX ngx_http_v3_module vulnerability CVE-2026-123007: NGINX ngx_http_v2_module vulnerability CVE-2026-123633: NGINX ngx_http_v2_module vulnerability CVE-2026-123634: NGINX resolver vulnerability For more information, see the nginx Security Advisories . AWS.summary: You can now use your Network Firewall with all its existing filtering capabilities and features as an explicit forward proxy. On Nov 25, 2025, AWS introduced Network Firewall proxy in public preview to help customers exert centralized security controls against data exfiltration and malware injection. At the time, the Network Firewall proxy was introduced as a standalone product, separate from Network Firewall transparent firewall and used its own separate proxy security policy.
